summary: This study investigates the factors influencing gut microbiota composition in healthy Japanese populations through 16S rRNA sequencing of fecal samples from two large cohorts. summary: The study investigates how oral administration of Blautia wexlerae improves obesity and T2DM by altering gut microbiota metabolism. A cross-sectional analysis of Japanese adults found inverse correlations between Blautia abundance and obesity/T2DM. Mouse experiments showed B. wexlerae reduced high-fat diet-induced metabolic issues through amino acid and carbohydrate metabolism pathways. The research highlights potential therapeutic strategies for metabolic disorders.

title: The association between gut microbiota development and maturation of intestinal bile acid metabolism in the first 3 y of healthy Japanese infants
summary: This study investigates how gut microbiota development correlates with intestinal bile acid (BA) metabolism in healthy Japanese infants during their first three years. Using fecal BA profiling, it identifies four BA types and tracks transitions from Con/Pri to Sec types as infants transition to solid foods. Using fecal samples from 40 healthy adults and elderly individuals, the research found lower IgA responses to certain bacterial taxa (e.g., Clostridiaceae, Enterobacteriaceae) in the elderly group, potentially contributing to shifts in microbial communities. Using longitudinal faecal samples from 12 infants, it identifies three distinct SCFA profile phases and links specific bacterial taxa (e.g., Clostridiales, Bifidobacterium) to SCFA production. summary: This study investigates how saprotrophic and ectomycorrhizal fungal richness vary along elevational gradients in cool-temperate montane forests. It finds that total and saprotrophic richness decrease with elevation, while ectomycorrhizal richness increases. Environmental factors like soil properties, climate, and plant communities influence these patterns, with source-sink dynamics driving contrasting elevational trends between fungal guilds.

summary: This study investigates the relationship between child weight gain trajectories and oral/gut microbiota composition in 226 two-year-olds. summary: This study investigates gut-derived biomarkers to identify PPI-associated dysbiosis and its link to liver-related mortality in cirrhotic patients. summary: This study investigates the relationship between intestinal microbiota and barrier function in preterm infants. It analyzes microbial composition in 45 quiescent CD patients over 2 years, finding that reduced microbial richness and specific taxonomic shifts (e.g., decreased Christensenellaceae/S24.7, increased Gemellaceae) correlate with flare risk. title: A framework for assessing 16S rRNA marker-gene survey data analysis methods using mixtures
summary: The paper presents a framework for evaluating 16S rRNA sequencing analysis methods using environmental sample mixtures. Results show DADA2 has higher false-negative rates while Mothur/QIIME have higher false-positives, but all pipelines align with expected relative abundances. The framework serves as a community resource for method assessment.
